name: Interbotix ViperX-300 6DOF
description: Trossen Robotics' largest X-Series research manipulator — a 6-DOF, DYNAMIXEL-servo arm with a 750mm reach and 750g payload, built around ROS/ROS 2 packages, MoveIt motion planning, and Gazebo simulation support.

sourcing: Specs sourced from Trossen Robotics' official product page (trossenrobotics.com/viperx-300) and its X-Series arm documentation (docs.trossenrobotics.com, vx300s specification page), including the full per-joint servo table. **Status:** as of this research, Trossen's own store lists the ViperX 300 S as sold out ("KIT-VIPX300-6DOF-OLD" in their SKU) with a note that a new-generation product line has replaced it and is available for pre-order — pricing here reflects the last listed price for this (now legacy) unit, not a current one. robotindex does not sell this product.

pricing.summary: Last listed at $6,742.95 on Trossen Robotics' own store before going out of stock — treat this as a historical rather than current price. The listing is marked sold out, with a notice that a "new generation" product line is available for pre-order as a replacement; no public specs or pricing for that successor were found, and Trossen directs interested buyers to contact sales directly.

editorial.heading: Sensors & Hardware
editorial.body: The ViperX-300 6DOF runs on 9 DYNAMIXEL smart servos — seven XM540-W270 units for waist, shoulder, elbow, wrist-angle, and forearm-roll, plus two XM430-W350 units for wrist rotation and the parallel gripper — at 4096-position resolution over a 1Mbps bus. Trossen ships full URDFs, MoveIt configs, and Gazebo support; the same stack powers ALOHA's bimanual teleoperation arms.

editorial.heading: Insights
editorial.body: The ViperX 300 6DOF ships with open CAD files and 3D-printable end-effectors, and Trossen documents its complete per-joint servo specs — a level of openness and repairability uncommon among comparable robotic arms. It also carries full ROS and ROS 2 support (MoveIt, Gazebo, Python API).

firmwareCommunity.note: Trossen Robotics' own official ROS/ROS 2 packages for the X-Series arm family, including the ViperX-300 — used as the follower-arm platform in Stanford's open-source ALOHA teleoperation system.
